name: Lyft Motion Prediction 1st Place — Multi-Modal Trajectory Forecasting from BEV Rasterization
summary: Multi-modal trajectory prediction from bird's-eye-view rasterized scene representations using EfficientNet/ResNet backbones with a custom 3-mode prediction head trained via negative log-likelihood loss.
dejargonized_summary: Predict where nearby cars will drive by converting road maps and vehicle histories into overhead images, feeding them through image-recognition neural networks that output three possible future paths with confidence scores.

inputs.name: hd_map_vectors
inputs.constraints: HD map vector data including lane boundaries, crosswalks, and traffic signals.

inputs.name: ego_trajectory_history
inputs.constraints: Shape (T_hist, 2+). Ego-vehicle past positions and headings.

inputs.name: agent_histories
inputs.constraints: Shape (N_agents, T_hist, 2+). Surrounding agents' past positions and headings.

outputs.name: predicted_trajectories
outputs.constraints: Shape (3, T_future, 2). Three predicted future trajectories (X/Y coordinates).

outputs.name: confidence_scores
outputs.constraints: Shape (3,). Confidence score for each predicted trajectory, summing to 1.

planning_constraints.subject: rasterization_before_cnn
planning_constraints.statement: BEV rasterization must precede CNN backbone ingestion.
planning_constraints.rationale: The CNN expects a fixed-size image tensor; vector map data must be rasterized into a BEV image first.

planning_constraints.subject: multimodal_head_design
planning_constraints.statement: The prediction head must output multiple trajectory modes with associated confidences.
planning_constraints.rationale: Single-mode prediction averages over possible futures, producing unrealistic trajectories. Multi-modal output allows the model to represent distinct maneuvers.

stages.name: BEV Rasterization
stages.description: Convert vector map data, ego-vehicle history, and agent history into a 3D bird's-eye-view image tensor using L5Kit rasterization. Each semantic layer (lanes, crosswalks, agents, ego) is rendered into separate channels.
stages.dejargonized_description: Draw an overhead picture of the road, nearby cars, and the ego vehicle's past path, encoding each element as a separate color channel in an image.

outputs.name: bev_image
outputs.constraints: Shape (C, H, W). Multi-channel BEV image tensor.

preconditions: Map data and trajectory histories are available and spatially aligned.
guarantees: Output is a fixed-size image tensor suitable for CNN input.
family_notes: Uses L5Kit's semantic rasterizer which renders each map element type into a separate channel.

stages.name: Temporal Stacking
stages.description: Stack multiple temporal frames of rasterized BEV images along the channel dimension to encode motion history in a single tensor.
stages.dejargonized_description: Layer overhead images from several consecutive time steps on top of each other so the network can see how things have been moving.

inputs.name: bev_image
inputs.constraints: Shape (C, H, W). Single-frame BEV image.

outputs.name: stacked_bev
outputs.constraints: Shape (C * T_frames, H, W). Multi-frame BEV tensor with temporal channels.

preconditions: Multiple consecutive BEV frames are available.
guarantees: Output encodes temporal context via channel stacking.

stages.name: CNN Backbone
stages.description: Pass the stacked BEV tensor through an EfficientNet-B7 or ResNet-50 backbone pretrained on ImageNet. The first convolutional layer is adapted to accept the expanded channel count.
stages.dejargonized_description: Run the layered overhead image through a powerful image-recognition network to extract meaningful spatial features.

inputs.name: stacked_bev
inputs.constraints: Shape (C * T_frames, H, W). Multi-frame BEV tensor.

outputs.name: backbone_features
outputs.constraints: Shape (B, D). Pooled feature vector from backbone.

preconditions: Input channels match the adapted first conv layer.
guarantees: Output is a fixed-length feature vector per sample.
family_notes: EfficientNet-B7 and ResNet-50 are used as complementary backbones for ensembling.

stages.name: Multimodal Prediction Head
stages.description: Custom output layer that takes backbone features and predicts 3 possible future trajectories (X/Y coordinates for each future timestep) and 3 associated confidence scores via softmax.
stages.dejargonized_description: A final layer that produces three candidate future paths for the vehicle along with how likely each path is.
guarantees: Confidences sum to 1 per sample. Three distinct trajectory modes produced.

stages.name: Multimodal NLL Loss
stages.description: Custom negative log-likelihood loss that selects the predicted trajectory closest to ground truth and penalizes the model for not assigning high confidence to that mode. Encourages mode specialization.
stages.dejargonized_description: A training objective that rewards the model for making at least one of its three predictions close to reality and for being confident about the right one.
preconditions: Predictions and ground truth are temporally aligned.
guarantees: Loss is differentiable and encourages mode diversity.
family_notes: This winner-take-all loss prevents mode collapse by only backpropagating through the best-matching mode.

stages.name: Trajectory Ensembling
stages.description: Average the trajectories of the highest-confidence predicted paths across multiple trained models (different backbones and seeds). Confidence scores are also averaged.
stages.dejargonized_description: Combine predictions from multiple trained models by averaging their best guesses to get a more reliable final prediction.

inputs.name: predicted_trajectories
inputs.constraints: List of (3, T_future, 2) trajectory arrays from each model.

inputs.name: confidence_scores
inputs.constraints: List of (3,) confidence arrays from each model.

preconditions: All models produce compatible output shapes.
guarantees: Ensembled output is smoother and more robust than any single model.

audit.rationale: 1st place Lyft Motion Prediction solution. BEV rasterization approach with multi-modal trajectory prediction using EfficientNet/ResNet backbones and custom NLL loss for mode diversity.
audit.dejargonized_summary: Predict where cars will drive by converting road maps and vehicle histories into overhead images, running them through image-recognition networks that output three possible paths with confidence scores.
provenance_notes: Source: Kaggle Lyft Motion Prediction 1st place solution (2020)
uncertainty_notes: The number of predicted modes (3) is fixed by competition rules; more modes may improve real-world performance.
BEV rasterization loses fine-grained vector map structure; vectorized approaches may outperform for some scenarios.
